name: TDC ADMET Half_Life_Obach
description: Predict the elimination half-life of a drug in humans (hours) from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint Half_Life_Obach of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the Spearman rank correlation between the predictions and the measured values of the test compounds, averaged over the five runs; higher is better, and only the order of the predictions counts.

sources.locator: Trend Analysis of a Database of Intravenous Pharmacokinetic Parameters in Humans for 670 Drug Compounds
Half Life, Obach et al.: regression, 667 drugs (ChEMBL deposit of the Obach data).

Huang et al. (2022), Artificial intelligence foundation for therapeutic science (Nat Chem Biol): the Therapeutics Data Commons paper linked from the TDC site, benchmark paper only; also arXiv 2102.09548, Therapeutics Data Commons: Machine Learning Datasets and Tasks for Drug Discovery and Development.

requirements.datasets: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_smiles, train_y, valid_smiles, valid_y, test_smiles, info) -> sequence of finite numbers, one per test molecule in the given order: the predicted value. train_smiles, valid_smiles and test_smiles are lists of SMILES strings, train_y and valid_y lists of numbers; info has name, metric, kind ('regression' or 'binary') and seed. Score: mean over the seeds 1 to 5 of the Spearman rank correlation between predictions and measured values on the test part, maximized.
notes: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

limitations: Leaders are large tuned ensembles or foundation-model fine-tunes.
Needs PyTDC and rdkit: not in .venv-tasks, so the evaluator restarts itself under tools/venv-admet (created by the README's setup steps).

Every scoring call of the candidate runs in the main suite's sandbox (a child process with an audit hook, 700 s and 6 GB for one call): it keeps a search from coming across the test labels and is not a security boundary against a candidate written to attack the evaluator.
One evaluation of the starting program took 130 s in the run of 2026-11-11, more than the arena's default limit of 120 s: raise AR_EVAL_TIMEOUT for this task.
The record was found in a hashed snapshot of its source; it is not replayed. See VALIDITY.md.

science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
science_relevance.reason: The cited paper(s) have the prediction or measurement of this property as their main objective; the task scores a structure-based predictor of the same property.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the human elimination half-life (hours) of a drug after intravenous dosing from its structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Half-life sets how long a drug acts and how often it must be dosed, so predicting it from structure helps select candidates with a workable dosing regimen.

papers.title: Trend Analysis of a Database of Intravenous Pharmacokinetic Parameters in Humans for 670 Drug Compounds
papers.task_relation: The task predicts the half-life values of this database from structure; the paper analyses the data and does not fit a predictor of the kind scored here.
papers.primary_goal: Assemble human intravenous pharmacokinetic parameters (clearance, volume of distribution, half-life) for 670 drugs and analyse their trends with structure and properties.
